editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece covering a multi-vendor announcement with five named speakers. Correctly separates independently-confirmed facts (the 26-repository count, corroborated by Phoronix) from single-source press-release claims.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 snapshots directly. source-0 (Linux Foundation press release) confirms every quoted phrase verbatim: the OPI self-description, the 'break down barriers' quote, the API layer description, the OPI Blueprints description, the white paper title and scope, and all four named quotes (Joshipura, Pullela, Moses, Horman) verbatim including titles/affiliations. One trivial source-side typo noted: the release has 'CPU/GPU//DPUs' (double slash); the article silently normalizes to 'CPU/GPU/DPUs', a reasonable typo correction, not a fidelity issue. source-1 (opiproject.org, the project's own site) confirms the Blueprint's OpenShift/F5 NGINX/Intel IPU E2100 stack details verbatim. source-2 (Phoronix) independently corroborates the 26-repository figure and the Nginx/Intel/Red Hat Blueprint attribution verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (repository count, vendor names, hardware model, speaker titles, summit date/location) trace verbatim to the cited sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral; the Analysis section is clearly framed as analysis, not asserted as fact.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate -- no prior archive coverage of OPI or this release.
recommendations: Added opiproject.org to config/source_allowlist.txt -- the OPI Project's own official site (a Linux Foundation initiative), used here as a legitimate primary source for its own release announcement, consistent with existing precedent for other Linux Foundation project domains (e.g. cncf.io, linkerd.io).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve. All quotes and specifics verified verbatim across all three sources; no corrections needed. The only automated finding (opiproject.org not on the allowlist) was resolved by adding the domain, which is clearly a legitimate first-party source.
